pairs.distinction: Rising prices squeeze my own budget; inequality is the gap between groups, which can grow even when prices are steady.
pairs.reason: Someone hit by prices and someone angry about the rich pulling away are naming different things, and either could pick one without the other.

pairs.distinction: Rent is one bill; rising costs are everything at once, from groceries to gas.
pairs.reason: Housing is the biggest cost for many people and deserves its own pain, while rising prices covers the rest of the budget.

pairs.distinction: One is not having children because of cost; the other is paying for care for children you already have.
pairs.reason: A person choosing whether to have kids and a parent paying a daycare bill are in different places, so each would pick one easily.

pairs.distinction: Rent is about the cost of housing for anyone; starting a family is about putting off kids, often because of housing.
pairs.reason: Housing costs are one reason people put off kids, but the pain someone names is either the rent or the family they can't start.

pairs.distinction: Rent is my own bill being too high; homelessness is seeing neighbors who have no home at all.
pairs.reason: Paying too much and having nowhere to live are different situations, even though high rent drives homelessness.

pairs.distinction: The safety net is about having nothing to catch you; homelessness is one place people land without it.
pairs.reason: A person worried about one bad month is naming something wider than people sleeping outside.
Being short on money is personal and rising prices is the shared cause, so the same squeeze shows up on both pages and the two should stay linked.

pairs.distinction: Inequality is the gap in money and wealth; opportunity is whether where you start decides where you end up.
pairs.reason: They often travel together, but someone can be bothered by the wealth gap today without naming mobility, and the other way around.

pairs.distinction: Childcare is the bill; parenting is being worn out by the work of raising kids.
pairs.reason: A parent who can't pay for daycare and a parent who is exhausted are naming different problems, even if both are true at once.
Student debt is a common kind of the debt people carry personally, so it belongs on both pages as two pains linked across them.

pairs.distinction: Rent is what housing costs; housing on the personal page is the state of the place, cramped, broken or noisy.
pairs.reason: Paying too much and living somewhere in bad shape are different complaints, and many people have only one of them.
High rent is the shared cause and fear of eviction is how it lands for one household, so the two stay linked across pages.
Seeing neighbors without a home and fearing I'll lose mine are the same issue seen from the street and from inside, so they stay linked across pages.

pairs.distinction: AI is one specific cause of job loss across society; layoffs is my own job being at risk for any reason.
pairs.reason: Someone worried about their own layoff may not be thinking about AI at all, and someone worried about AI may feel secure in their own job.

pairs.distinction: AI is a worry about jobs disappearing in the future; unemployment is not finding work now.
pairs.reason: One is a fear about where work is heading and the other is a present search, so a person can tell them apart at once.

pairs.distinction: The safety net covers any fall, from job loss to illness; medical bills are the cost of care itself.
pairs.reason: Medical bills are one way people fall, but the worry about healthcare costs stands on its own under health.
Seeing people near me go hungry and worrying my own food won't last are the same issue at two scales, so they stay linked across pages.

pairs.distinction: Decline is the town losing jobs, shops and people; neighbors is not knowing the people who are still here.
pairs.reason: A thriving city can be full of strangers and a shrinking town can be close-knit, so these are different losses.

pairs.distinction: Decline is the town emptying out; local control is who makes the decisions about it.
pairs.reason: Decisions made far away can be one cause of decline, but someone watching shops close is naming the loss, not the governance.
